answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so influence depends on paths from trusted seeds, not claimed identities. If jade, beacon, and zenith anchor those walks, a sybil cluster with few links to honest nodes has low conductance: only a small share of walk mass crosses its sparse external cut. When votes are weighted by that mass, conductance bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, limiting capture without proving each participant’s identity.
